scheduler_candidates.name: INTELLIGENCE_UPDATE
scheduler_candidates.reason: Claim/Hypothesis/Intelligence-Object upserts are triggered synchronously from the same acquisition/admission flow already running in n7_live_acquisition (upsert_claim/upsert_intelligence_object are called from within the acquisition+admission call chain, not from an independent cron). A separate schedule would race against the acquisition job writing the same sidecars rather than add real value; no evidence of a queued/batched update need that the current synchronous call chain doesn't already serve.

scheduler_candidates.name: REPORT_REBUILD
scheduler_candidates.reason: report_engine.build_report() and atomic_publish.py's REPORT_JSON/HTML/PDF publish boundaries are invoked at build time (CI build step), not as a standing schedule; the Failure Isolation Matrix (Deliverable 1) found this path is per-artifact, atomic, and safe to re-run on every CI build. Adding a separate cron for 'report rebuild' would just re-run the same build step on a second clock with no new capability.

scheduler_candidates.name: PUBLIC_PUBLISH
scheduler_candidates.reason: public_delivery.build_public_intelligence_pages() already runs at CI build time as part of the same site build that daily.yml drives; it is per-report fault-isolated (Deliverable 1) and atomic (os.replace). No standing gap that a dedicated publish-only schedule would close beyond what the existing build-on-push/cron already provides.

pre_gate_G1_G15.condition: Failure Isolation READY (any FAILED stage fails this gate)
pre_gate_G1_G15.evidence: Deliverable 1 (intel/phase_n9/n9b_failure_isolation_matrix.json): 10/13 stages READY, 3/13 PARTIAL (PARSE, RELATION, INTELLIGENCE_BUILD -- non-atomic shared-sidecar writes, a real but bounded gap), 0/13 FAILED. Since the explicit Pre-Gate condition is 'any FAILED stage fails this gate' and there are zero FAILED stages, G8 itself is READY, though the 3 PARTIAL stages are carried forward honestly as a known residual gap (see overall caveat below).

queue_model.py:NON_RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUS_CODES=(401,403) + retry_with_backoff() refuses retry for these; general 5xx/transient failures get bounded exponential backoff (max_retries=4). This exact 4xx-vs-5xx distinction was also the subject of a dedicated prior-phase fix (commit c004619: 'N-9 Sections 18/22/25: 4xx-vs-5xx retry fix').

queue_model.Job.dispatch() tracks dispatched job_ids to avoid double-execution; claim/hypothesis/intelligence-object upserts are all keyed by deterministic sha256-derived IDs (_claim_id/_hypothesis_id/_intelligence_id) so re-running the same acquisition+admission input produces the same key and an upsert rather than a duplicate.

upsert_* functions merge into an existing record keyed by ID, which is consistent with a NO_CHANGE input being a no-op update, but no explicit NO_CHANGE status/code path was located and verified end-to-end in this phase's time budget -- PARTIAL rather than fabricated READY.

public_delivery.discover_real_reports()/build_public_intelligence_pages() iterate over all real reports each build rather than a diffed affected-only set; this is safe (atomic, fault-isolated per Deliverable 1) but is a full rebuild, not an affected-only incremental build, so this condition is not fully met as literally stated.

public_delivery.py's per-report build routes through report_engine/atomic_publish.py's GENERATE->TEMP WRITE->VALIDATE->ATOMIC REPLACE (os.replace), confirmed in Deliverable 1 (HTML/PUBLIC_PUBLISH stages, both READY).

research_rights_model.py keeps access_status/rights_status independent and defaults every new record to UNKNOWN_RIGHTS/UNKNOWN_ACCESS/FULLTEXT_*_ALLOWED=False (fail-closed); intel/operator_workspace/operator_boundary_contract.json explicitly documents and this audit (Deliverable 2) verified compliance: no full text, credentials, or private material found in site/, including site/operator/**.

n9b_before_snapshot.json (Deliverable 0, prior commit) and n9b_after_snapshot.json (this phase, below) both hash claims.json/hypotheses.json/intelligence_objects.json/statistical_evidence.json; the after-snapshot in this phase confirms these hashes are unchanged by this phase's own work (Deliverables 1-4 only wrote new files under intel/phase_n9/ and ran read-only test/measurement scripts).

final_decision_rationale: All 15 conditions must be READY for a PASS; 3 of 15 (G7 evidence yield consistency not re-verified this phase, G11 NO_CHANGE handling not located/verified end-to-end, G12 public publish is full-rebuild not affected-only) are PARTIAL rather than READY. Per the standing instruction never to force a conditional pass, the honest result is NOT_READY. This NOT_READY applies to wiring any NEW scheduler (INTELLIGENCE_UPDATE / REPORT_REBUILD / PUBLIC_PUBLISH), all three of which were independently judged NO_NEW_SCHEDULER_REQUIRED on their own merits above -- i.e. the gate's NOT_READY result and the 'no new scheduler needed' conclusion are consistent, not contradictory: there is no candidate scheduler this phase recommends wiring, and even if there were, the Pre-Gate is not fully green yet. LIVE_ACQUISITION needs no gate decision since it already exists and was not duplicated.
